# Minimum tool bag for a station visit

This is the floor, not the full kit — what has to be in the bag before
anyone sets off on a weekend round, regardless of how quick the planned
visit is meant to be. It exists because "I'll just pop up and check one
thing" has turned into an hour of improvising with the wrong tools often
enough that the group agreed on a minimum rather than trusting judgement on
the day.

## The tools themselves

A multi-bit screwdriver covering both the enclosure fixings and the
terminal block screws, a small adjustable spanner for the mast clamp
bolts, wire strippers and a handful of spare crimp connectors, and
electrical tape. Nothing exotic — the point of the list is that it's all
small enough to fit in one bag and common enough that nobody has an excuse
to leave it behind.

## Beyond tools

A torch that isn't the one on a phone, since phone torches drain the
battery you might need for the return call and don't survive being held in
your teeth for ten minutes. Spare desiccant sachets and a cloth, now
standard after how often a box needs drying out on the spot rather than
scheduled as a separate job. The debug cable pair, in case a station's
behaviour on site doesn't match what the dashboard is showing and a proper
look at the logger is needed there and then rather than guessed at from
the road below.

## What's deliberately not on this list

A full spares kit — spare gauges, spare batteries, spare radios — isn't
part of the minimum, because carrying every possible spare on every round
turns a station visit into moving a warehouse up a hillside, and most
weekend rounds don't need any of it. Spares get added to the bag for a
specific visit based on what that visit is actually for, on top of this
floor, not instead of thinking about it.

## Checking the bag

Whoever is heading out checks the bag against this list before leaving,
not from memory. It takes under a minute and has caught more than one
missing screwdriver bit over the life of this rule, which is a cheap trade
for not standing at the base of a mast an hour from home with the wrong
kit.
